canvas-01.description: Sheet 1 of the September 1920 Netcong atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the centre of Netcong between Lake Musconetcong and the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad. North is to the upper left of the page. In the upper part, Main Street runs down from the lake past the Stanhope Methodist Episcopal Church and the Palace Moving Picture Theatre, with Ledgewood Avenue (the Morris County Turnpike) and Allen Avenue branching to the east and Mechanic Street running north-east along the railroad to Stoll Street. Around the junction of Main and Mechanic is the business block: W. E. Bostedo's general store, the Mansion House, a bank, drug, clothing and grocery stores, the fire house and a garage. River Avenue and Furnace Road lie to the west. The railroad crosses the sheet diagonally with its many tracks, the passenger and freight depots, coal pockets, D. S. Drake's building supplies yard, C. H. Lunger's feed house and the Sussex Branch leaving to the south. South of the tracks Main Street continues past the Imperial Hotel and Down's Arbitrary to Center and Church Streets, with St. Michael's Roman Catholic Church and Union Hall; Mount Olive Avenue in the south-west has the Standard Oil Company of New Jersey's tanks and Salmon Brothers, contractors. A. P. Villa and Brothers' works stand by the Sussex Branch at the bottom of the sheet. Housing is mostly frame dwellings with outbuildings and automobile sheds. The upper right of the page carries the title, water and fire notes, the key, a location map, a key map of the three sheets and the specials index; these are not part of the georeferenced area.
notes: Old Mechanic Street is today's Maple Avenue; it meets Ledgewood Avenue at the Allen Terrace junction.
Old Furnace Road is today's Bank Street, old River Avenue today's Jenny Lind Street and old Mount Olive Avenue today's Flanders Road.
Main Street south of the railroad is now US 46 and lies several metres west of the drawn street; its junctions with Center and Church Streets were not used as control.
The modern junction of Allen Street and Ledgewood Avenue lies about 13 m from the drawn one and was not used.
Placed from four points (two detected Main Street junctions, a railroad crossing on Flanders Road and a hand-picked Ledgewood Avenue / Maple Avenue junction); low to medium confidence.

Printed sheet 1 (canvas labelled Index). 100 ft to an inch, north to the upper left. Map of central Netcong (Main, Mechanic, Ledgewood Av, Allen Av, River, Furnace Rd, Center, Church, Mt. Olive Av, D.L.&W. RR); the upper right carries title, notes, key, location map, key map and specials index, cut out of the mask. One part. Modern streets here have moved (US 46 on Main south of the tracks, Allen St, Jenny Lind St): placed from 4 points.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 of the September 1920 Netcong atlas, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the north-eastern part of Netcong between Lake Musconetcong and the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad. North points to the left of the page. Dell Avenue, Allen Avenue and Lake Street form the blocks along the lake shore on the left; College Road and Prospect cross in an X in the middle of the sheet, with Hillside Avenue, Kings Road and Ridge Road at the top and Stoll Street (Mechanic) curving along the railroad on the right. Ledgewood Avenue runs along the bottom to a steel bridge over the tracks, continuing as the Morris County Turnpike. Most of the area is laid out in house lots, many still vacant: the large blocks 7, 9 and 10 are only partly built. Netcong Public School stands on College Road; a base ball park, an ice house, a garage with buried gasoline tanks, a bottling works not in operation and a vulcanizing shop are among the few non-residential buildings. The railroad yard and a private water pipe from a reservoir run along the right side, and a strip beyond the tracks repeats the outlines of West, Union and North Streets from sheet 3; that strip is left out of the georeferenced area. Dwellings are mostly two-storey frame houses with sheds and automobile garages.
notes: Old Prospect Road is today's Prospect Street and old Lake is Lake Street; Allen Avenue is Allen Street.
Netcong Public School is on College Road.
The modern junction of Allen Street and Hillside Avenue lies about 17 m from the drawn one and was not used.

The strip east of the railroad (West, Union and North Streets) is cut out of the mask: it repeats sheet 3, and through this sheet's fit it lay about 20 m west of where sheet 3 and the modern parcels put it.

100 ft to an inch, north to the left. North-east Netcong: Dell Av, Allen Av, Lake, College Rd, Prospect, Hillside Av, Kings Rd, Ridge Rd, Stoll (Mechanic), Ledgewood Av; strip beyond the railroad repeats West/Union/North Sts of sheet 3. One part. The strip east of the railroad (West/Union/North Sts) is cut out of the mask (repeats sheet 3; about 20 m off through this sheet's fit).

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of sheet 3 of the September 1920 Netcong atlas shows the village of Port Morris, in Roxbury Township about one and three quarter miles east of Netcong. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch on the label, but the fit to modern streets shows it drawn about 7 percent larger than that. The part covers the blocks between Lake Musconetcong and the Morris Canal: Palmer Street on the west, Washington (Lake) Street, Main or Morris Street and Center Street running east across the sheet, Davis Street in the middle and Hill and Forest Streets at the east edge, with Canal Street along the canal bank. Two roads leave Palmer Street to the south-west towards a concrete bridge over a creek. The village is residential, with frame dwellings, coops and sheds on long narrow lots; between Main and Center Streets east of Davis stand the Port Morris Hotel and a motion picture house, and near Palmer Street the public school, the Methodist Episcopal church and a general store with the post office; south of Center Street are another general store and an automobile repair shop with a buried gasoline tank. Much of the land north of Main Street east of Davis is open. The part continues east in the inset at the top right of the sheet.
notes: Forest Street is today's Willow Street.
Drawn about 7 percent larger than its stated scale of 100 feet to an inch (fitted 4.35 px/ft against 4.04 to 4.16 on the other sheets).

100 ft to an inch. Three parts: part 1 (bottom, main) Port Morris (Palmer, Washington (Lake), Main or Morris, Center, Davis, Hill, Forest, Canal), drawn about 7 percent above its stated scale; part 2 (top left) Netcong east of the railroad (West, Union, Barone, North Sts, Ledgewood Av), north to the left; part 3 (top right) inset continuing Port Morris east along Center St beyond Hill and Forest, same scale and rotation as part 1, placed from three points carried from part 1 (modern Center St / Willow St node about 20 m from the drawn Center / Forest junction, not used).

sheet-3-2.description: The upper left part of sheet 3 of the September 1920 Netcong atlas shows the eastern edge of Netcong beyond the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, at 100 feet to an inch, with north to the left of the page. West Street (arbitrary name) runs up the left side beside the railroad tracks, and Union, Barone and North Streets run east from it to Ledgewood Avenue, which crosses the right side of the part diagonally. The blocks 16, 17 and 18 are divided into narrow house lots with mostly two-storey frame dwellings, a few concrete-block and stone houses, sheds and coops; a grocery stands at the corner of West and North Streets. Large blocks 15 and 19 to the north and east are empty. A private water pipe runs along Barone Street and a four-inch water pipe along North Street.
notes: Old West Street is today's West Railroad Avenue, whose line lies along the west edge of the drawn street; its junction with North Street was not used.
Modern Union Street runs north from West Railroad Avenue; the drawn Union Street along block 16 has no modern counterpart east of the junction.
Placed from four points; medium confidence.

100 ft to an inch. sheet-3-3.description: The upper right part of sheet 3 of the September 1920 Netcong atlas is an inset continuing the Port Morris map to the east, at the same scale and orientation as the main Port Morris part. It shows Center Street from Hill Street (arbitrary name) east past Forest Street (arbitrary name), with block 20 north of Center Street and block 21 between Center Street and the Morris Canal. Center Street is lined with small frame dwellings, mostly two storeys, with a few sheds; one dwelling is marked dilapidated, and the east end of the block carries a no exposure note. The upper part of the inset is empty except for Forest Street running north; notes on Port Morris printed there, left outside the georeferenced area, give population 750, prevailing winds west, no fire apparatus, 56 street lights, no water works and Center Street improved.
notes: Forest Street is today's Willow Street; the modern Center Street / Willow Street junction lies about 20 m from where the main Port Morris part places the drawn one, so it was not used.

Placed from three points carried from the main Port Morris part (sheet 3, part 1): the Hill Street / Center Street junction, the corner of Forest and Center Streets and the south end of Hill Street; an exact fit with no spare point, low to medium confidence.
